title: Behind the Display
introduction:
我关注的是时尚圈的变化，以及背后的工业化生产和消费文化。现在很多东西都可以被快速大量地生产出来，一个流行趋势出现后很快就会被复制，再不断被新的趋势取代，随着现在时代的快速发展这也改变了我们对“美”的理解。

我觉得现在我们现在对自己的形象和身份的塑造很容易受到社交媒体上流行趋势和群体审美的影响，我们会不断观察别人去调整自己的穿着打扮，我们会去模仿去复制相似的外表和生活方式。有时候我们觉得自己是在选择喜欢的东西，但其实这些选择也可能已经受到周围环境的影响。

我想关注的就是这种重复被复制和变化之间的关系，时尚不仅仅是在改变我们的外表，也在影响我们对自己的自我理解。这种大规模生产消费和流行趋势之间的关系以及这些东西背后反映出当代人的物质和精神追求。
introduction-en:
This project began with my observations of the contrast between luxury retail spaces and large-scale production in China. Through carefully arranged displays, brand symbols, and lighting, boutiques create an image of desirability. The revisions, material processing, and assembly-line work that support this image often remain out of sight. I am interested in how objects acquire different meanings and values as they move between these spaces. 

The installation brings two contrasting settings together. On one side, transparent display cases, a clothes hanger, a jewellery stand, a red velvet seat, and an invented brand identity recreate the visual language of a luxury boutique. On the other, repeatedly reworked sketches, marked fabric, and assemblages incorporating buttons and zips on a conveyor belt evoke the repetition and disorder of production. Separately lit within the same photographic studio, both settings are revealed as deliberately constructed scenes. 

By placing display and production within a shared field of view, I ask what makes a luxury object desirable: its material qualities, or the imagined identity constructed around it?
